title: Tala-Informed Cycle / Accent Displacement

source_refs.author: Indian music theory and ethnomusicology scholarship
source_refs.title: Tala, cyclical meter, and sam/khali relations
source_refs.cultural_context: North and South Asian rhythmic traditions

observed_structure: a recurring cycle establishes an expected point of return
accent, action, or visual emphasis shifts away from that point
the delayed or altered return changes anticipation while preserving the cycle
cinematic_affordances: editing cycle repeats with one displaced cut
gesture lands before or after the established visual downbeat
sound and movement reunite at a later return point
empty beat functions as structural absence
cultural_scope: South Asian rhythmic provenance must be retained; use only the formal relation of cycle, emphasis, absence, and return unless culturally specific consultation supports more
misuse_risks: claiming equivalence among distinct tala systems
decorative rhythmic complexity without dramatic consequence
transferable_structure: a stable cycle gains dramatic pressure when emphasis moves and later returns under altered agency
non_transferable_surface: imitating specific compositions, instruments, devotional contexts, or naming a tala without accurate structural use
